lesson_title: Getting to know Git and the terminal

task.title: The first repository
task.description: In the learning terminal, Git is not configured yet, and you are in your home folder. Write the commands one per line: 1) Check the Git version. 2) Globally set your name (user.name), email (user.email, with the @ symbol) and the main branch main (init.defaultBranch). 3) Create a folder portfolio, go into it and create a repository. 4) Create a file README.md with the text # Portfolio. 5) Look at the state of the repository with git status.
task.starter_code:
# Write the commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments.
# You are in the home folder ~, Git is not configured yet.

# 1. Git version

# 2. Name, email and the main branch main (globally)

# 3. Folder portfolio, go into it, repository

# 4. File README.md with the text # Portfolio

# 5. State of the repository

tests.name: The name is set globally
tests.fail: git config --global user.name "First Last" - put the name in quotes if it has a space.

tests.name: The email is set globally and contains @
The default main branch is main
The repository ~/portfolio is created
tests.fail: mkdir portfolio, then cd portfolio, then git init.

tests.name: The repository is not created in the home folder
tests.fail: Run git init inside the portfolio folder, not in ~.

tests.name: The repository branch is main
tests.fail: First the setting init.defaultBranch main, then git init.

tests.name: README.md is created in the project folder
tests.fail: echo "# Portfolio" > README.md - after cd portfolio.

tests.name: README.md contains the text # Portfolio
tests.fail: Put the text in quotes: echo "# Portfolio" > README.md

tests.name: git status is run inside the repository
tests.fail: git status goes last, when you are already in the portfolio folder.

tests.name: There are no commits yet
tests.fail: Commits are the topic of lesson 2: you don't need git add and git commit here.

tests.name: The script runs without internal errors
tests.fail: Check the quotes in your commands.

hints: Example: git config --global user.name "Anna Karimova" - the name goes in quotes.
The order matters: first init.defaultBranch main, then git init.
mkdir portfolio, cd portfolio, git init - three separate commands.

questions.question: What is a version control system?
options: A program that stores the history of changes to files and lets you go back to any version
questions.explanation: Git stores snapshots of the project - commits - and lets you compare them and go back to them.

questions.question: Match each term with its description.
pairs: A program on your computer that stores the version history
A website for storing repositories and working in teams
A snapshot of project files with the author's signature
A project folder together with its commit history
questions.explanation: Git works locally, GitHub is a website; a commit is a snapshot, a repository is a project with its history.

questions.question: What does the pwd command show?
questions.explanation: pwd stands for print working directory: the path to the current folder.

questions.question: Which commands change the current folder?
questions.explanation: Only cd changes the folder. mkdir creates a folder but doesn't go into it; ls shows the contents.

questions.question:
The file index.html had 50 lines. What is left after echo "

Hi

" > index.html?
options: 50 lines and a new line at the end
An error: the file already exists
questions.explanation: The > sign replaces the whole contents of the file.

questions.question: Which command shows the contents of a folder including hidden files such as .git? Type the whole command.
questions.explanation: The -a (all) option shows files whose names start with a dot.

questions.question: What does the --global option mean in git config --global user.name "Anna"?
options: Everyone on the internet will see the name
The setting applies to all repositories of this user
The setting applies only to the current repository
The name will be saved on GitHub
questions.explanation: --global means for all repositories of the user on this computer. Without it, only for the current repository.

questions.question: Complete the command so that the main branch of new repositories is called main: git config --global ________ main
Where does Git store the commit history of a repository?
questions.explanation: The whole history, the branches and the settings of the repository are in the .git folder.

questions.question: What is true about git status?
options: It shows new and changed files
It saves changes to the history
You can run it as many times as you like - it doesn't change anything
questions.explanation: git status only shows the state. git commit is what saves changes.

questions.question: Match each message with its cause.
pairs: A Git command was run outside a repository
The folder has files that Git doesn't track yet
The repository has no commits yet
bash: cd: sitee: No such file or directory
questions.explanation: Git and terminal messages tell you what went wrong.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you run git init in your home folder ~?
options: Git will treat all your files as part of the project
Your home folder will be deleted
The command will run very slowly
questions.explanation: One project - one repository. You create a repository in the project folder.
